name: NGC 1852 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 1852, an intermediate-age star cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc1852-hubble
story: NGC 1852 is an intermediate-age star cluster in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way. Its main-sequence turnoff is broadened, one of the clues that such clusters are not the simple single-age crowds once assumed.

claims.text: NGC 1852 is an intermediate-age Large Magellanic Cloud cluster
NGC 1852 was a target of program 12257 on Magellanic Cloud star clusters
The Large Magellanic Cloud is a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way
Such clusters challenge the idea of simple stellar populations
NGC 1852 shows a broadened main-sequence turnoff
The pointing was chosen to overlap earlier Hubble ACS images
NGC 1852 is a relatively massive cluster
